sources.title: Publishers say no to AI scrapers, block bots at server level
sources.span: 'About 5.6 million websites presently have added OpenAI's GPTBot to the disallow list in their robots.txt file, up from about 3.3 million at the start of July 2025.' ClaudeBot reported blocked at about 5.8 million sites, up from 3.2 million in early July. Tollbit cited as reporting 13.26% of AI-bot requests ignored robots.txt in Q2 2025, up from 3.3% in Q4 2024.

sources.title: Cloudflare's new policy pushes AI companies to pay for publishers' content
sources.span: 'Starting on September 15, 2026, Cloudflare's default settings will block "mixed-use" crawlers from any pages that host ads.' 'These changes to the defaults will apply to new Cloudflare customers, new sites set up by existing customers, and all existing free customers.' Stated rationale: 'Website owners want their content to be discoverable via search and through AI services as well, but they want protections against having their intellectual property given away for free.' A 'Pay Per Use' model is described as succeeding the earlier pay-per-crawl experiment.

sources.title: Hacker News comment search: zero trust / VPN replacement
sources.span: Item 45981893 (2025-11-19): reports better uptime from a hyperscaler WAF than from an incumbent edge vendor over ~1.5 years, and a comparable competing quote via a reseller. Item 44852206 (2025-08-10): installing an access client on ephemeral CI compute is impractical; VPNs assume on-premises networks. Item 46160621 (2025-12-05): mid-market firms may not need a dedicated edge vendor, and organisations often prefer flat-rate to usage-based billing. sources.title: 18 November 2025 outage: vendor postmortem and independent reliability analyses
sources.publisher: Cloudflare blog; independent commentary from Gremlin and Purdue Polytechnic newsroom
sources.span: Snippet-level. A permissions change caused a bot-management feature file to grow beyond expected size and propagate network-wide; core traffic delivery failed from 11:20 UTC for over four hours, affecting many dependent services. Independent commentary summarised as: if an architecture assumes the provider is always there, the provider is by definition a single point of failure, and internal service interdependencies allow cascading effects.
